“My heart breaks for you and your family,” Hilton wrote. “Presley was truly one of a kind, and I feel so lucky to have known him. I’ll always remember him with so much love.”
Presley was signed by IMG Models when he was 15 and modelled for brands including Burberry, Dolce & Gabbana and Bottega Veneta.
He spoke frequently about his struggles with depression and substance abuse.

articles.title: 'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
articles.summary: A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests

blocks.text: A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests on Saturday.
Dramatic footage shared online shows the 19th-century building engulfed in flames, with the spire of its clock tower later collapsing.

On Sunday, stunned residents watched as firefighters, who had battled the blaze through the night, assessed the building's structural integrity. Officials have not yet confirmed whether the town hall is at risk of collapse.
"Damaging heritage buildings because you're angry with the government is selfish", one resident told the BBC.
BBC correspondent Chris Bockman reports from Limoges.

articles.title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
articles.summary: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table.

"I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine," Trump said on his Truth Social messaging platform, adding that he didn't want to "do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table".
Trump blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky deepened.
Zelensky told NBC News on Sunday that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a "historic mistake".

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev has responded to Trump's order by calling it "an important and truly historic moment", and saying the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.
Trump also claimed in his Truth Social post that Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did", adding "he could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now".
Zelensky has pushed for an end to fighting, and has repeatedly said that Putin doesn't want peace, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.
Since then, Zelensky declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing a European Union summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Putin.

articles.title: Ebola: Kenya cases rise to 8, spreads to 8th Congo province
articles.summary: A senior health official in Kenya said there have now been 8 Ebola infections in the country, while in DR Congo the disease has spread to an eighth province.

image.caption: Kenya has been on heightened alert due to a major Ebola outbreak in Central Africa [FILE: October 7, 2026]Image: Andrew Kasuku/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Kenya's Health Ministry on Sunday confirmed another case of Ebola, bringing the number of confirmed infections in the country to eight.
News of another patient in the East African state came as health officials in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) reported that the outbreak there had spread to an eighth province.
What Kenya's health director general said
"Today, 38 people were tested, and one tested positive for Ebola," Health Ministry Director-General Dr. Patrick Amoth said in an ​interview on Kenya's Citizen TV.
"He is a 49-year-old man ​who is not a healthcare worker. He developed ​fever, headache and muscle pain," Amoth said.
He went on to explain that the latest case was a patient attendant who cleaned utensils and linen and had likely been exposed to Kenya's first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month.
Amoth said patients in quarantine were being tested after developing symptoms and that the other six patients were stable after receiving supportive treatment. The first patient died on October 5.
Kenya has been on a heightened state of alert as a major outbreak of the highly contagious disease spread in Congo in central Africa.
Ebola now in 8th province in Congo
Also on Sunday, authorities in DRC said that the Ebola outbreak had spread to an eighth province in the north.
Congo's Health Ministry said that two cases including a death were recorded in Nord-Ubangi province which borders the Central African Republic (CAR).

"We see pockets of Ebola generally going down, but unfortunately geographically it's spreading out," said World Health Organization Regional Director for Africa Mohamed Yakub Janabi in an interview with The Associated Press in Beni, eastern Congo, on Friday.
It's currently the deadliest outbreak in Congo's history with authorities recording at least 9,400 cases, including over 4,500 deaths, in the outbreak declared in mid-May.
The current epidemic is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare type of Ebola that has no approved vaccine or treatment.

Ebola is spread between people by direct contact with bodily fluids. It can cause fever, fatigue, and muscle pain, followed by vomiting and diarrhea. Some patients also develop internal or external bleeding.
Congo's Ebola crisis: Fear, mistrust and a growing outbreak

articles.title: Canada's Einarson wins 7th Grand Slam of Curling title, 1st since 2024
articles.summary: Kerri Einarson won her seventh Grand Slam of Curling title and first in two years, beating South Korea's Team Kang 6-3 in the women's final at the Co-op Invitational in Victoria on Sunday.

image.caption: Canadian skip Kerri Einarson, pictured at the world championships last March in Calgary. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Breaking
Kerri Einarson won her seventh Grand Slam of Curling title and first in two years, beating South Korea's Team Kang 6-3 in the women's final at the Co-op Invitational in Victoria on Sunday.
New-look rink never trailed en route to 1st Grand Slam title together
Einarson's new-look rink never trailed en route to its first Grand Slam title together. Her team from Gimli, Man., consists of third Shannon Birchard, second Karlee Burgess and lead Jocelyn Peterman.

Team Kang, skipped by Kim Kyeong-ae, tied the game at 2-2 in the third end after Einarson scored singles in the first two, but the five-time Tournament of Hearts champion responded by scoring two with her final shot in the fourth.
Einarson added another deuce in the sixth after holding Kim to a single in the fifth.
Kerri Einarson captures 7th Grand Slam title with victory over Team Kang at Co-op Invitational
Top-ranked Yannick Schwaller of Switzerland will face Norway’s Magnus Ramsfjell in the men’s final later Sunday.

The Co-op Invitational is the first of five stops on a newly compressed Grand Slam of Curling tour that will be completed before Christmas. The next stop is the Masters in Medicine Hat, Alta., from Nov. 3-8.
More to come.

articles.title: Liberals and Conservatives urge 'decisive' Alberta referendum vote to remain in Canada
articles.summary: With Alberta's referendum vote on Monday, federal Liberals and Conservatives are on the same page, each hoping to put to bed any question of the province's place in Canada.

image.caption: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre, left, speaks about national unity in Calgary on Friday, the day after Prime Minister Mark Carney, right, attends a Forever Canadian rally in Calgary. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics
With Alberta's referendum vote on Monday, federal Liberals and Conservatives are on the same page, each hoping to put to bed any question of the province's place in Canada.
Ottawa wants to put separatism to bed, but polls show most Albertans have doubts
In the final days leading to the Alberta referendum, federal Liberals and Conservatives are on the same page, each hoping to put to bed any question of the province's place in Canada.
On Monday, Albertans will vote on whether they want to remain a province in Canada or start the legal process toward holding a binding referendum on leaving the country.
In their respective campaigning efforts, the government and the Official Opposition have urged Albertans to decisively vote to remain.

items: 'Vote like Canada depends on it,' Carney says at Calgary rally ahead of Alberta referendum

blocks.text: Prime Minister Mark Carney headlined a rally in Calgary on Thursday where he called for "a decisive result on Monday to settle this question."

Conservative MP Dane Lloyd — the caucus lead for the party's own Conservatives for Canada campaign — made an equivalent appeal in an exclusive interview on Rosemary Barton Live that aired Sunday morning.
"We need to ensure that every patriotic Canadian, Albertan gets out to vote so that we can have an overwhelmingly decisive vote for a stronger Alberta within a united Canada," Lloyd said.

Liberal MP Corey Hogan said there's likely no "magic number" that would put the issue of Alberta separation to rest. He told CBC's Rosemary Barton that the measure for success is whether there will be "an understanding from all political actors in this province that we can never do this again."
'Albertans are not quitters,' Poilievre tells Calgary conference

Recent polling from Abacus Data suggests that 68 per cent of voters would opt to keep Alberta a province of Canada, while 24 per cent would vote to start the legal process to hold a binding referendum on separating from the country.

The Abacus survey, which was conducted from Oct. 7 to 13, polled 1,021 Alberta voters. The survey's data was weighted according to census data, to ensure its sample matched Alberta's population. The margin of error for a comparable probability-based random sample of the same size is approximately plus or minus 3.1 percentage points, 19 times out of 20.

Still, the polling suggests that most voters don't expect Monday's referendum will reliably bookend the issue. Abacus found that 61 per cent of the survey's respondents said at some point, they expect to vote again on Alberta separation after Monday.
According to Hogan, who represents the riding of Calgary Confederation, a separatist sentiment is just a reality in Alberta.
"Alberta separatism has been a thing my entire life," he said.

items: Danielle Smith has said no to a second referendum. But that decision might not be hers to make
Poilievre urges Albertans to embrace Canada: 'We don’t take our ball and go home'

blocks.text: "It's always been a reality worth addressing, it's always been a problem that there's a number of people in Alberta who have concerns with the country as a whole," Hogan said. "But it's not realistic to say this is going to go to zero, because it's never been at zero in Alberta."

Hogan added that "we need to make sure that there are political consequences to this," suggesting Albertans have become increasingly frustrated with their provincial government for carrying out the referendum process.

"We're going to have to see where this all is on Oct. 20," he said. "I'm certainly not calling the game at this particular moment, but it's very important that we as a province have a serious talk about how we ended up here in the first place."
For their part, Conservatives point to the Liberal government as a main irritant in Alberta's relationship with Canada.

Lloyd, who represents the Alberta riding of Parkland in Parliament, said he held roundtable discussions with Albertans as part of the Conservatives for Canada campaign, "and the message that I heard that was overwhelmingly clear was that people don't have a problem with Canada, they have a problem with Ottawa."
FULL SPEECH | Carney attends Forever Canadian rally in Calgary

At the same time, the current federal government hasn't been shy about acknowledging Ottawa's role in Albertan discontent. During his Thursday rally, Carney said that growing up in Alberta, "I remember how Ottawa made Albertans feel like our resources weren't our own."
"This is about Alberta feeling like its contributions haven't always been respected," Hogan said.
"We need to make sure that this whole country sees this whole country and that we are thinking about this whole country as we build policy for this country."
What about the other nine questions?
Listed before the consequential 10th question concerning a binding separation referendum, Monday's ballot notably includes nine others.

The first nine questions are focused on immigration and constitutional reform, including a query on whether Alberta should take more control over immigration, the responsibility for which is currently shared between the federal and provincial governments in Canada.
Quebec is alone in having distinct powers regarding the selection of its immigrants.

items: Who else besides Danielle Smith is saying 'yes to the nine' in Alberta's referendum?
Carney says Albertans should vote ‘No to the Nine’ in referendum

blocks.text: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith has advocated for voters to choose "yes" on the ballot's first nine questions, while Carney was clear in urging Albertans to reject them.
Asked where the Conservatives stand on the first nine questions, Lloyd said the party's campaign has been "laser-focused" on the issue of a separation referendum "and that issue alone."

"Immigration has always involved federal-provincial conversations, and I think that they've been largely productive and largely fruitful," the Liberals' Hogan said. "We don't need people trying to hold guns to each other's heads to have constructive relationships in Canada."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
David Cummings is a reporter for CBC News.

articles.title: Inside Chicago's battle against the synthetic drugs flooding the US
articles.summary: A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis. The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from the frontlines in South Side, Chicago, where…

blocks.text: Warning: This video contains descriptions of drug-taking and distressing images
A new wave of synthetic drugs is sweeping across the United States, raising fear of a worsening drug crisis.
Earlier this year, President Donald Trump pledged a crackdown on drug cartels, proscribing many as terrorist organisations.
Drug overdose deaths have fallen from a peak of around 110,000 in 2022, down to roughly 70,000 last year.

However, America's decades-long drug crisis may be accelerating and authorities are increasingly concerned about cheaper, more powerful synthetic drugs, including an animal tranquilliser called tranq.
The BBC's Quentin Sommerville reports from the frontlines in South Side, Chicago, where communities are battling the crisis.
Camera journalist: Darren Conway

articles.title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
articles.summary: Presley Gerber's death in September is being investigated as a suspected overdose.

blocks.text: Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him. "We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."
The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California. Police said officials are investigating his death as a suspected overdose.
Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.
Crawford wrote in the post on Sunday: "We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years."
"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," she also posted.
"Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia," she wrote in closing, with an emoji of angel wings.
The tribute also listed the dates of his birth and death.

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner lists Gerber's case as pending additional investigation. The Santa Monica Police Department has said there is no indication foul play was involved in his death.

Gerber's sister Kaia also dedicated a post to him on Sunday which included a video of the two siblings as children dancing together, a photo of them standing near the ocean, and a four-page letter to "prez" typed out on a blue background.
In the letter, she said she had been scared of getting her ears pierced, so "you went first".
"But when I held the earring they took from your body, all I could think was: That belongs to you," she wrote.

"I am learning how to love you when I cannot see you," she also wrote. "How to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you. How to be your sister in a world that I can't reach for you in," she wrote.
In recent years, Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use and frequently posted videos on Instagram himself for what he called "Mental Health Mondays".
His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.
If you're affected by any of the issues in this article you can find details of organisations who can help via the BBC Action Line.
Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide, external, external.

articles.title: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama ignores calls to resign amid violent clashes
articles.summary: Anti-government protesters continued calls for Edi Rama to step down as violent clashes between demonstrators and police again took place.

image.caption: Violence erupted for a sixth day as protesters continued calls for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step downImage: Hameraldi Agolli/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Student-led protests continued in Albania for a sixth day with continued demands for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.
Despite those calls, Rama is refusing to step down, saying the demonstrations were not a threat to government but rather a threat to Albania's ambition of accession to the European Union.

blocks.caption: Protesters gathered again at noon in front of the education ministry chanting "Rama, resign" amid a tense standoff with policeImage: Hameraldi Agolli/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What Rama said

"I ​am not being challenged, the government is not being challenged, a government majority or a winning party in the elections is not being challenged but a path is being challenged, a mission is being challenged," Rama said in a live address on Facebook.
"Albanians need to think ​very clearly: Do they want this, do they want that, or do they want the EU?” Rama asked.
Rama ruled out resigning and said that the protests are the "work of an outside hand."
Earlier in the week Rama ruled out resigning, saying that governments were changed through elections.

Student-led demonstrations, spurred by discontent over alleged government corruption, unemployment and poor education standards, have rocked central Tirana and spread to other cities in the past week.

blocks.caption: Riot police use water cannon and rubber bullets after demonstrators threw Molotov cocktails and threw rocks and fireworksImage: Boris Grdanoski/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Continued clashes between protesters and police
On Sunday, hundreds gathered outside the Education Ministry, chanting "Rama resign!" and threw rocks ​at riot police who responded with tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets.
The protests come at a difficult for Albania as it is among a group of Balkan states seeking to join the EU by 2030.
There have been calls for calm from Brussels amid the violent protests. The European Commission in Sunday condemned the use of ⁠violence ⁠in Tirana and othern cities.
The commission added that it welcomed the Albanian authorities' ​commitment that the right to protest will ​be protected.
Police target students in Tirana as Albania protests grow

articles.title: Israel: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of elections
articles.summary: The US president said he supports Israel's current prime minister in the country's elections on October 27. But polls say Netanyahu and his far-right partners currently lack the majority to secure a…

image.caption: US President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin NetanyahuImage: Allison Bailey/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has announced his "complete and total" endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Israel will hold parliamentary elections on October 27, with opinion polls suggesting neither Netanyahu nor the opposition will manage to secure the 61 seats needed to form a coalition.
"Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu," Trump posted on his Truth Social account.
Iran war at center of Trump announcement
According to Trump, Netanyahu is a "Great Warrior Prime Minister," also commending him for his role in the war against Iran.
"BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!" Trump added.
Netanyahu thanked the US leader for his "tremendous support."
"Together we will complete the mission," Netanyahu posted on his X account, alluding to the joint campaign by the two countries against Iran.

blocks.caption: Netanyahu has been vocal in his objection to Iran's nuclear programImage: Richard Drew/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Trump said the US would be alone in the war against Iran if Netanyahu were not re-elected, also mentioning the chant often sung at events by Iran's Revolutionary Guards that calls for both the US' and Israel's death, also labeling the two countries "the big and small Satans."
"If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so," Trump said.
Netanyahu opponent reacts
The war between Israel, the US and Iran began in February and resulted in Tehran blocking some global oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.
Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main challenger, reacted to Trump's endorsement by saying the Israeli public are the only ones who decide who is the country's next leader.
Speaking at an event in Tel Aviv, Eisenkot voiced his appreciation of Trump's "large contribution" to Israel's security.
"But Israel is a democratic state," he said, adding that the US administration will learn to work with whichever government the public decides on.
Netanyahu boasts Trump friendship once again
This is not the first time Netanyahu's election campaign has invoked Trump's support to augment the Israeli leader's international status.

In 2019, Netanyahu's Likud party posted billboards showing the Israeli leader shaking hands with Trump during the latter's first term as US president, as well as with Russian President Vladimir Putin, describing Netanyahu as a leader of a "different league."

Netanyahu is the longest serving prime minister in Israel's history. Much of Israeli society is divided on his far-right coalition's role in the failure to foresee and prevent the October 7 terrorist attack by Islamist Palestinian group Hamasand its affiliates in Gaza, in which some 1,200 Israelis were killed.

Netanyahu has refused to establish a state inquiry with the authority to look into government documents and summon ministers and officials to testify. Instead, the prime minister wants a commission with less authority to see confidential documents and with no authority to force testimonies by the country's leading politicians and officials.

blocks.caption: Israeli opposition have been protesting against Benjamin Netanyahu's "failure" to prevent the October 7 attacksImage: Aviv Atlas/REUTERS

blocks.text: Another point of contention is Israel's war in Gaza that followed the attack, in which some 74,000 Palestinians have been killed.

Despite repeatedly promising a "total victory" after the war began, opposition supporters believe Netanyahu failed to deliver, with Hamas still in charge of many parts of the Gaza Strip. Netanyahu and his coalition partners have also promised to support what they called the "wilful migration" of Gaza residents, while also deepening Israel's hold on its territories in the West Bank, which is largely considered illegal under international law.
Other issues at the center of Israel's elections are the conscription of young ultraorthodox men into the military, the cost of living, and Israel's international status.
Netanyahu's final campaign? — Israel heads to the polls

articles.title: Guardian reporter filmed masked militants seconds before West Bank attack on French mayor
articles.summary:
New video footage of Israeli settler assault on European delegation as Netanyahu attempts to raise doubt

Hours after

blocks.text: Hours after Israeli militants attacked a delegation of European diplomats, French clerics and a visiting mayor in the occupied West Bank, Israel’s leader, Benjamin Netanyahu, responded by questioning the delegation’s account of the assault.

“Serious accusations require serious evidence” was the all-caps headline of a social media post from the office of the prime minister. As news of the attack spread globally there was no pledge to find those accountable and bring them to justice.

Instead Netanyahu’s team dismissed video of Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, on the ground grimacing in pain and shock, photos of the smashed window of a diplomatic car, and footage of masked men threatening diplomats and activists with sticks.
“These images alone do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility,” the statement said, warning of “concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel”.

The prime minister’s office went on to cast doubt on the integrity of senior French, Belgian and Polish diplomats in Jerusalem and clergy from the Catholic church who witnessed and reported the attack.

“We call on the public and responsible journalists to demand verifiable evidence, reject hearsay and refuse to turn unproven allegations into a collective indictment of the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria [the occupied West Bank],” it said.

Footage below filmed by the Guardian (no audio) shows the moments before Israeli settlers attacked the French mayor Bernard Baudoux, who was in the Palestinian town of Taybeh with a delegation of European diplomats. A second clip shows the immediate aftermath of the attack. The final section shows one group of settlers attacking the car carrying Baudoux and others.
Verifying the details of attacks can be painstaking journalistic work, seeking out eyewitness accounts, photos and videos for confirmation.

But this weekend the Guardian was in Taybeh, and witnessed the masked militants speeding up a hill in order to attack diplomats and French visitors who had spent a morning peacefully harvesting olives with Palestinians who own the groves.

Shortly after 1pm, they were warned that settlers had attacked Palestinians harvesting olives nearby. Keen to avoid confrontation, the group decided to leave and were approaching their vehicles as the militants closed in, masked, menacing and brandishing sticks.

The Guardian filmed the moments before Baudoux was assaulted, showing him approaching an SUV with his wife and Vincent Dollmann, the archbishop of Cambrai, escorted by diplomatic security. Our vehicle pulled away, making room for the two parked by the road to follow.
Moments later the settlers attacked, apparently determined not only to force the foreigners to flee but to extract a price for joining Palestinians on their land.

It was clear the group contained foreign dignitaries because the cars had diplomatic plates, and Baudoux was apparently targeted for his nationality, because he was wearing his mayor’s sash of office. One of the attackers aggressively shouted “France, France” before pushing him to the ground, eyewitnesses said.

Metadata from that video shows there were just 22 seconds between the last shot of Baudoux remonstrating with his attackers and footage of him slumped on the ground taken by activists in the second car.
The embassy security team then helped him into the vehicle but the attack continued as they drove off. Footage filmed from the hillside opposite shows the settlers attacking the SUV as pulls away.

The force of their blows smashed one of the reinforced windows at the back of the car, which can be seen intact in the first video. A photo of the crumpled pane taken minutes later in the relative safety of Taybeh shows the force of the impact.
If the militant settlers had broken one of the windows next to the passengers, it is unlikely those inside would have escaped injuries.

blocks.caption: Former Israeli ambassadors and employees demonstrated outside the foreign ministry, demanding the prime minister and his government ‘Stop Jewish Terrorism. It’s in your hands’. Photograph: Quique Kierszenbaum/The Guardian

blocks.text: Israeli authorities have repeatedly attempted to obfuscate details of attacks on Palestinians and undermine survivor or witness accounts.
For the prime minister to deploy the same tactics on senior diplomats from European allies – however strained their current relationship – marks a new embrace of isolationist extremism.

A day earlier the American photojournalist Heidi Levine was hospitalised after a brutal attack by Israeli militants blocking the Palestinian olive harvest in another village. Netanyahu’s office described it as an “alleged assault” and a “disputed incident” adding “the facts … remain unclear and are under investigation”.
The message from the very top of Israel’s government, that the state was reluctant to impose consequences or seek justice for that attack, may have emboldened the attackers on Saturday.

blocks.caption: The protest outside the foreign ministry in Jerusalem drew a response from conservative passersby. Photograph: Quique Kierszenbaum/The Guardian

blocks.text: There was one unprecedented response in Jerusalem, however. On Sunday, more than a dozen of Israel’s top former diplomats gathered outside the foreign ministry where they had all worked for decades for an unprecedented protest.

Two former directors general, one deputy director general and a host of ambassadors held up signs calling for action on the campaign of terror by Israelis against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
“Bibi [Netanyahu], foreign minister [Gideon] Sa’ar. Stop Jewish Terrorism. It’s in your hands,” read one banner.

articles.title: Flydubai captain describes blocking axe blows as co-pilot attacked him
articles.summary:
Capt Smit Machchhar said he screamed for help as he reached to open the cockpit door on flight FZ1073

The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash…

blocks.text: The captain of a flydubai flight who was attacked by a co-pilot who intended to crash the plane has described ⁠blocking axe blows to his head and screaming for help as he reached to open the cockpit door.

Capt Smit ⁠Machchhar has been hailed ⁠as a ​hero for his role in averting disaster on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv last month, helping to thwart what the UAE ⁠attorney general has said was an attempted suicide attack by the co-pilot who had intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion airport.

Speaking in an interview with ⁠The National newspaper from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi, his head and left arm bandaged, Machchhar ​said that when the first blow landed, ‌he thought something had gone “horribly ‌wrong with the aircraft structure” before quickly realising he was being attacked and things had “taken a drastic turn”.
“The ‌next thought was I need to get help in here,” he said. “My immediate action was to free myself from the seatbelts and I tried to just block the blows as much as I could.”

He pointed to his arm that was wounded as he defended himself. “The blows were coming on the head. Immediately my ‌hand went to the knob which opens the door and [I was] screaming for my colleagues, screaming his name. I believe that was the first time when I ​lost my consciousness.”

blocks.caption: Dubai’s Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, left, visited Capt Smit Machchhar in hospital in Abu Dhabi, UAE.  Photograph: Government of Dubai Media Office/AP

blocks.text: Flight FZ1073 was in Saudi airspace when the co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe, an item typically kept in the cockpit for emergency use.

The incident caused the airliner to plunge 16,000 ft (4,900m) in 30 seconds before the attacker was overwhelmed and two other pilots who were ⁠on board landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The suspect, an Omani ​national, was transferred to the ​UAE, flydubai’s home country.
The plan was ​inspired by the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors ​said as a ‌result of their criminal ​investigation, which was launched on ​1 October.
Machchhar said he heard the cockpit door opening and screaming “between my colleague and the guy”. He said the scariest thing he felt was the aircraft nose “steeply going down”.
“I was not very sure that I’ll make it out alive from this. Did I give up? No.”

articles.title: Canada's Dabrowski, Brazil's Stefani capture Wuhan Open women's doubles title
articles.summary: Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and Brazilian partner Luisa Stefani captured the women's doubles title Sunday at the Wuhan Open tennis tournament in Wuhan, China.

image.caption: Ottawa's Gabriela Dabrowski, right, and Luisa Stefani of Brazil pose with the trophy after defeating Storm Hunter of Australia and Katerina Siniakova of Czechia 7-5, 6-4 in the women's doubles final at the Wuhan Open on Sunday in Wuhan, China. (Chinatopix Via/China Out/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Tennis·Recap
Canada's Gabriela Dabrowski and Brazilian partner Luisa Stefani captured the women's doubles title Sunday at the Wuhan Open tennis tournament in Wuhan, China.
Top seeds defeat 3rd-seeded duo of Australia's Hunter, Czechia's Siniakova 7-5, 6-4
The No. 1 seeds defeated the third-seeded team of Australian Storm Hunter and Czech Katerina Siniakova 7-5, 6-4 in the final. Hunter and Siniakova were defending champions.
The win was the sixth of the season for Dabrowski, of Ottawa, and Stefani. They also earned an eighth title as a team and third in a row.
Canada's Dabrowski and Brazilian partner Stefani capture 7th career WTA doubles tournament title
Dabrowski and Stefani also improved their career record to 79-19 and qualified for the season-ending WTA final next month.
Dabrowski captured a 26th career doubles title.
"I'm really pleased with where we are and where our level is," Dabrowski said. "So it's really nice to see it pay off in results consistently throughout the season."

items: Gabriela Dabrowski claims 25th tour-level doubles title of her career at China Open

blocks.text: Dabrowski and Stefan had more aces (five to none) and fewer double faults (three to four) than their opponents. They also registered five breaks in 19 opportunities.
Hunter and Siniakova converted three-of-eight break chances.
Dabrowski and Stefani broke early to build a 4-1 lead in the first set before Hunter and Siniakova rallied to tie the score. The top seeds broke again in the 12th game to take the opening set.
They broke twice in the second set while surrendering their serve once to complete a victory in one hour 32 minutes.
With files from The Canadian Press

articles.title: Saudi Arabia sends skyscraper employees home amid Houthi threats
articles.summary: Riyadh's Kingdom Center tower's management told the people employed there to work from home "until further notice," without giving a reason. This comes as Houthi attacks escalate.

image.caption: The Kingdom Center is one of Saudi Arabia's tallest buildingsImage: Markus Mainka/Aviation-Stock/IMAGO

blocks.text: The Kingdom Center skyscraper in Riyadh told people employed there to work from home due to possible attacks by Yemen's Houthirebels.
The 99-storey tower is one of Saudi Arabia's tallest buildings.

Kingdom Center made working from home "mandatory" with no reason given. The new order is effective immediately and will be in power until further notice, the building's management told tenants, AFP reported.
Among the building's tenants are important financial institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, as well as wealth management company Merril Lynch.
At the building's foot is a shopping center, which will remain open for now.
Attacks increase

Studies in schools across Saudi capital Riyadh and the surrounding areas will take place online for a second week, with the city's King Khalid International Airport still being closed after a Houthi attack resulted in 13 casualties.
The conflict between the Saudi-led coalition and Iran-backed Islamist group Houthis has continued to escalate, with the coalition reporting its first military deaths since the escalation's beginning.

Two helicopter pilots were killed near the Yemen border due to a "technical malfunction," the coalition said, with the Houthis earlier announcing the downing of an Apache helicopter "belonging to the Saudi enemy," the group said.

blocks.caption: The Houthis have carried out attacks on international airports in Saudi ArabiaImage: Social Media/REUTERS

blocks.text: Conflict flares up again

On the Saudi side, two drones were intercepted over Riyadh overnight, with a third being shot down over the country's Eastern Province, a known oil-rich area, according to the authorities in the country.
Two ballistic missiles were also intercepted in Saudi Arabia's south.

The two sides have been confronting each other on various intensities over the past decade. After a four-year ceasefire, the conflict between the two sides saw an escalation after the Yemen-based Islamist militia took over strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis have targeted oil facilities, tankers and Riyadh's international airport, with the coalition carrying out strikes on Houthi areas.
Saudi Arabia on the backfoot in the war against the Houthis

articles.title: Meloni backs police after cost-of-living protests turn violent in Italian cities
articles.summary: Anger over living costs and low wages has brought Italians onto the streets. A major union has called a general strike for November 20.

image.caption: Clashes broke out in Milan during demonstrations against high living costs and low wagesImage: Stefano Porta/LaPresse/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Sunday condemned rioting during cost-of-living protests, expressing solidarity with police after clashes in several cities.
The violence broke out during cost-of-living demonstrations on Saturday, leaving at least four police officers and 20 demonstrators injured in Milan.
The unrest comes amid anger over high prices, stagnant real wages and a shortage of affordable housing in major cities.
What happened during the protests?
In Milan, black-clad, masked youths threw fireworks and bottles at police and erected barricades in the central Piazza Duomo, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.
Police initially withdrew to await reinforcements and later used tear gas to clear the square. Some 50 young people were arrested, about half of them minors, according to ANSA.
Clashes also broke out in Turin, Bologna and Bergamo. Police in Bologna used water cannon and made four arrests, all minors, with seven people reported to prosecutors.
How did Italy's PM Meloni respond?
Meloni expressed solidarity with police on Sunday, condemning criminals who she said exploited demonstrations to provoke confrontations and "sow chaos."
Italy tightens restrictions on the right to protest
"Demonstrating is a right, but setting our cities on fire is not," she said.
Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala also condemned the violence while acknowledging the grievances behind the demonstrations.
"The reasons for the protest were understandable. The violence against police and the serious damage to the city, however, cannot be justified," he said.
Why were people demonstrating?
Protesters rallied against high living costs and low wages, with households facing expensive fuel and difficulty finding affordable housing.
In Rome, thousands joined a demonstration organized by the Italian General Confederation of Labour (CGIL). Its leader, Maurizio Landini, announced a general strike for November 20.
The violence came as similar demonstrations in France descended into rioting, arson and looting, with more than 1,800 people arrested nationwide.

articles.title: China taking advantage of VP impeachment raps?
articles.summary: The Chinese ambassador’s provocative remarks against the Philippine government and its officials may actually be a ploy of Beijing to create more internal political havoc on the highly divisive…

blocks.text: Headlines
October 19, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Chinese ambassador’s provocative remarks against the Philippine government and its officials may actually be a ploy of Beijing to create more internal political havoc on the highly divisive impeachment issue of Vice President Sara Duterte, according to a former lawmaker.

“Is China simply pursuing its aggressive maritime agenda, or is it also taking advantage of our political divisions to weaken our resolve? These are questions our national security officials must examine,” former Surigao del Norte congressman Robert Ace Barbers said.

The House of Representatives’ impeachment adviser also stressed that while timing alone does not prove a deliberate connection, the possibility that China could “exploit domestic political tensions to advance its strategic interests cannot be dismissed without proper scrutiny.”
“The impeachment proceedings are an internal constitutional process. China has no business exploiting our political differences to advance its interests in our waters,” Barbers said.

He warned that a nation preoccupied with internal political battles risks losing focus on external threats. China could benefit if the impeachment controversy deepens divisions among Filipinos and distracts the public from developments in the West Philippine Sea (WPS).
From the administration’s perspective, Duterte has been very lenient and is actually pro-China.

Barbers said the government must determine whether the timing and patterns of Chinese activities point to a broader strategy. Any assessment, he emphasized, must be supported by credible intelligence and verifiable evidence – not political speculation.

He urged Filipinos, regardless of political allegiance, to remain vigilant against possible foreign interference and resist efforts to turn domestic disagreements into national vulnerabilities, like the highly sensitive issue of China’s encroachment into the WPS.

“Whether coincidence or calculated strategy, China’s actions demand scrutiny. We may disagree on politics, but defending our sovereignty and protecting our national interests must unite us all,” Barbers said.
As far as Rep. Leila de Lima is concerned, Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan’s statement basically says “we are stronger, so be grateful that we don’t use our might to crush you.”

“This is absolutely the language of a liar and an invader who lacks sincerity in promoting peace. They may be mightier, but the world knows who has already won in our fight for sovereign rights over the WPS. And they know the consequences if they resort to using force against us,” De Lima said.

“If they truly love peace, then they should get out of our territory and stop harassing our countrymen and depriving our fishermen of their livelihoods. They are the ones encroaching on our territory,” the former senator and justice secretary pointed out.

“But being a bully, China will not stop threatening us. We will also keep defending what is ours. They cannot threaten us, because we Filipinos will never ever allow ourselves to be oppressed, conquered or subjugated,” De Lima said.

articles.title: DENR expands watershed repairs, forest protection vs El Niño
articles.summary: The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has stepped up its mitigation efforts on watershed restoration and forest protection to address water supply concerns amid El Niño.

blocks.text: October 19, 2026 | 12:00am
People visit the Pililla Wind Farm in Rizal yesterday. The 54-megawatt wind farm features 27 wind turbines that generate renewable electricity for the Luzon grid.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has stepped up its mitigation efforts on watershed restoration and forest protection to address water supply concerns amid El Niño.

The DENR said it is expanding forest protection patrols and accelerating targeted reforestation across critical watersheds nationwide to help forests retain water, regulate streamflow, reduce soil erosion and recharge depleted aquifers.
The effort combines the restoration of degraded and fire-damaged areas with measures to keep newly planted trees alive and protect existing forests.

DENR chief Juan Miguel Cuna said the DENR is mobilizing local communities, civil society groups, Indigenous Cultural Communities and field personnel to maintain forest cover and strengthen the natural systems that support water security.
In Central Luzon, DENR is carrying out forest restoration activities across critical watersheds in Aurora, Bataan, Nueva Ecija and Zambales.

In Nueva Ecija, the Manila Bay Site Coordinating and Management Office is inspecting established narra plantations to assess seedling survival rates and soil moisture conditions under elevated heat indices.
In the Bicol region, DENR offices are combining new tree-growing activities with measures to improve the survival of existing plantations.

In Masbate, the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office partnered with the Integrated Bar of the Philippines Bicol Chapter, local government units and the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office to plant more than 16,750 indigenous and mangrove seedlings across 50 hectares in the province’s second and third districts.

In Camarines Norte, DENR field officers require contractors under the Enhanced National Greening Program to establish plantations to replace dead seedlings and follow supplemental watering schedules to improve the tree survival under dry conditions.
In the Caraga region, field units are prioritizing the rehabilitation of fire-affected peatlands, riverbanks and protected areas.

Protecting existing watersheds is also essential to securing water supplies, as in Davao City, the Apo Agua Infrastructura Inc. and the Obu-Manuvu Indigenous Cultural Community conducted a comprehensive habitat assessment of the Panigan-Tamugan Sub-watershed, which serves as the city’s primary source of potable water.

In another development, the Department of Labor and Employment is preparing advisories on workplace safety during El Niño, with measures meant to protect workers from extreme heat without cutting their pay.
Senseless remedy
The Alliance of Concerned Teachers yesterday called the decision of the Department of Education to allow students to wear sleeveless shirts as a “senseless remedy” to the effects of super El Niño.

In a statement, ACT chairperson Ruby Bernardo said the Marcos administration and DepEd are resorting to superficial measures instead of addressing the systemic neglect that leaves public schools ill-equipped to withstand extreme weather and climate-related hazards. — Delon Porcalla, Christine Boton, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: US ambassador to Israel denounces West Bank settler attack on US photojournalist
articles.summary:
Mike Huckabee calls for arrest and prosecution of those responsible as Heidi Levine, 63, recovers in hospital in Israel

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler…

blocks.text: The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror” and called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible.

Levine, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives in occupied West Bank towns.

The 63-year-old photographer, who is in a hospital in Petah Tikva near Tel Aviv recovering from hand surgery, broken ribs and other injuries she sustained in the attack, said she was beaten for more than 10 minutes by the settlers, who also stole her camera, passport and phone.

“I was attacked, pushed to the ground,” Levine said. “Luckily, I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking and kicking me.” She added the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened to save her.

Huckabee, a rightwing ally of President Donald Trump with a track record of hardline, pro-Israel rhetoric, was notably blunt in his condemnation of what he called the “vicious and cowardly attack” on Levine. In a post on X on Saturday, he noted that she was a US citizen who had been clearly identifiable as a journalist.

“We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this,” Huckabee added. “Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonorable act of senseless violence.”

Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has been ambiguous in addressing Levine’s assault, condemning “violence against anyone” but referring to the attack as “alleged” and saying its circumstances remain unclear.

The attack on the Palestinian farmers and Levine was followed on Saturday by another outbreak of settler violence directed against European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of the French city of Cambrai, who were visiting the occupied West Bank.

Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was wearing his red, white and blue sash of office and attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates when he was assaulted and knocked to the ground. A masked militant shouted “Vive la France!” as he launched the attack, a witness said. Badoux’s wife, and Vincent Dollmann, the archbishop of Cambrai, were also threatened by the group of seven men, some armed with clubs.

The group had joined the olive harvest on lands belonging to the Christian town of Taybeh, along with the French consul general in Jerusalem, his wife and other diplomats, and the Belgian and Polish consuls.
“I think that if settlers are behaving like this, there is a tolerance on the part of the Israeli government,” Baudoux told Agence France-Presse after he was attacked.
“The whole world needs to know what’s happening. For me, I’ll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here.”

Violence is surging ahead of bitterly fought elections to be held on 27 October, with Palestinians’ annual olive harvest being repeatedly disrupted by Israeli settlers as Netanyahu seeks to shore up his pro-settlement rightwing base.

France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, has called on Israel to “urgently halt criminal violence” and to arrest those responsible for attacking Baudoux. The EU has condemned the attack and urged “full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians, including during the ongoing olive harvest season, as well as against journalists”.
The European Commission executive vice-president, Teresa Ribera, went further, posting an interview with Levine in hospital and adding the caption: “They want no witnesses.”
Israel’s foreign ministry has condemned the attack on the diplomats and Israeli police promised to open an investigation.
President Isaac Herzog, who holds a mostly ceremonial role, called Levine in hospital on Saturday, saying the attack was “outrageous and shocking” and was weighing on his conscience.

Netanyahu’s main rival in the elections, the former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, criticised the prime minister over the violence, saying it was “burning away the little legitimacy the state of Israel still possesses”. He described the attacks as “Jewish terrorism, under the auspices of the Israeli government”.

Trump officially endorsed Netanyahu for re-election in a post on his Truth Social network on Sunday, hailing him as “a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran”. He added: “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself.”
The Washington Post has reiterated its call for a full and transparent investigation into the attack on Levine, even though Israel rarely investigates settler violence fully.
Yesh Din, an Israeli rights group, says around 94% of investigations into settler violence since 2005 have ended without an indictment, with just 3% leading to full or partial convictions.
The Associated Press and Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Ukraine apologizes after a suspected drone crashes in Lithuania, damaging a moving car.
articles.summary: Debris has damaged a moving car in Lithuania, where NATO jets were scrambled. Kyiv says Russian jamming may have diverted drones targeting Russia.

image.caption: Italian Eurofighters operating under NATO command were scrambled in response to the drone incident in Lithuania (FILE 04/03/2024)Image: Armando Babani/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ukraine apologized Sunday after a suspected drone crashed in northern Lithuania, prompting shelter warnings and the deployment of NATO fighter jets.
The incident raised fresh concerns about the spillover of Russia's war against Ukraine into NATO territory, although the drone's origin and whether it carried explosives remained under investigation.
What happened in Lithuania?
Lithuanian authorities told residents in central and northern regions to seek shelter Sunday morning after detecting an unidentified flying object.
Debris damaged a moving civilian vehicle, but no one was injured, national crisis management centre chief Vilmantas Vitkauskas told Lithuanian radio.
Defense Minister Robertas Kaunas said the drone probably entered from neighboring Poland. He proposed a joint investigation with Warsaw.
Two Italian Eurofighter jets operating under NATO command were deployed, a NATO spokesperson said. Kaunas said weather conditions prevented visual identification.
Have similar incidents happened before?
Lithuania and its Baltic neighbors have experienced several drone incursions during the war.
Ukrainian drones intended to strike targets in northwestern Russia have previously strayed into Baltic airspace and crashed. Russian-made drones have also entered Lithuania from Belarus.
Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda described Sunday's incident as another example of the war spilling onto NATO's eastern flank.

articles.title: Pope appears in public for first time since surgery
articles.summary: After undergoing a lung operation, the pope said he will resume his duties gradually. There is no "clinical reason" for his South America trip not to go ahead, his surgeon said.

image.caption: The pope looked physically well as he addressed the crowdsImage: Alessandra Tarantino/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV said he would resume his duties "gradually" as he addressed the crowd for the first time since his lung cancer surgery.
Part of the pope's right lung was removed as part of the operation, which took place at the Gemelli Hospital in Rome. He was discharged on Saturday.

The Catholic leader thanked those who prayed for him while he was hospitalized, saying he would "gradually assume" his activities as the crowd cheered upon seeing him appearing. The 71-year-old spoke normally and looked physically well.
The people said the "delicate phase" is behind him, thanking "God and your prayers" for it and also expressing his gratitude to the medical staff at the Rome hospital.

During his time at hospital, the pope still made his worries about the Ukrainian civilian population clear. He held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, urging for a ceasefire in the Ukrainian town of Oleshky, located on the front line.
Putin reacted by saying Ukraine is responsible for the situation.
Recovery in ten days
According to his surgeon, the pontiff is in an "absolutely satisfactory clinical condition," with his full recovery probably taking some ten days.

blocks.caption: The crowds cheered as the pope made his first appearance Image: Gregorio Borgia/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "His determination to achieve a very quick and very effective recovery from every point of view was really commendable," Dr. Stefano Margaritora told Vatican News.
Margaritora said the tumor had been found during a routine X-ray checkup, while also saying the operation to remove it was "routine."

The pope's next major assignment would be his trip to South America, in which visits to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru are planned. The trip should take place between November 6 and 17. Speaking about the pope's recovery, Dr. Margaritora said he sees "no clinical reason" why the trip should be called off.
Testing of the tumor and related lymph nodes was underway, with the results determining whether Pope Leo needs additional medical treatment.
The 71-year-old Pope Leo was born in Chicago. He's been in his role since May 2025.

articles.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
articles.summary: An expedition to a remote Pacific island hoping to uncover the American aviator's wreckage was on hold for three days.

blocks.text: Image source, Purdue University
Sirisha Bandla (right), pictured with expedition lead Steve Schultz, said the crew was "really excited"
A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean has resumed after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days.

A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery.
The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate.
Rough seas and strong winds forced the team to remain on their research vessel for three days, until the weather cleared on Sunday.
"We are finally getting off the ship and able to land on Nikumaroro," Sirisha Bandla, a technology specialist who is part of the expedition, said in a video update from the deck of the Marin Mainiku.
The researchers arrived at the uninhabited atoll last week and began an underwater survey of the area of interest.

But the weather - powered by strong El Niño conditions in the Pacific - has so far prevented them from beginning a second of three phases, in which underwater objects will be probed to determine their depth and sediment will be dredged.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean while piloting her Electra plane in 1937

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean while piloting her Electra plane in 1937
"We're working to get everything done today if we can," Bandla said. "The crew's really excited."
Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her twin-engine Lockheed Electra when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea on 2 July 1937.
From there, she and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to travel towards Hawaii and then finally back to California.
But her plane vanished without a trace while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote, uninhabited coral island near Nikumaroro, to refuel.
One theory is that Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.

Images of the so-called Taraia Object - which Purdue University says is visible in photography dating back to 1938 - show what could be the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters, though other explorers remain sceptical.

blocks.caption: Image caption, A satellite image of the so-called Taraia Object in a lagoon on Nikumaroro

blocks.text: Image source, Archaeological Legacy Institute
A satellite image of the so-called Taraia Object in a lagoon on Nikumaroro
Interest in the expedition prompted New Zealand's Air Force Museum to publish, external previously unseen reconnaissance images of Nikumaroro on Friday.

While the Taraia Object is not obviously visible in any of the black-and-white slides, taken in 1938 from a seaplane, they do show the beached wreck of the SS Norwich City, a British merchant vessel that ran aground on the island during a storm in 1929, killing 11.
Purdue, which with the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) is spearheading the expedition, said the incident demonstrated the risks surrounding the island.
To get into the atoll's lagoon, a boat has to navigate through a narrow gap created in the reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.
But the university said wind gusts of up to 27 knots (31mph) present around the island until Sunday meant the transport boat could be knocked into the reef by crashing waves.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Images from 1938 released by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand this week show Nikumaroro - then Gardner Island - with the SS Norwich City wreck in the bottom right corner

blocks.text: Image source, RNZAF
Images from 1938 released by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand this week show Nikumaroro - then Gardner Island - with the SS Norwich City wreck in the bottom right corner
However, it said the Norwich City wreck may lend credence to the researchers' theory.

Purdue said a 15-year-old in Florida reported hearing Earhart's voice repeating "New York City" over her father's shortwave radio shortly after the aviator vanished. Proponents of the castaway theory argue this may have been a misunderstanding of Earhart giving her location as near the Norwich City.

As a result of the three-day hold, the research team has extended the expedition time to complete its fieldwork and has yet to indicate whether they had found any promising evidence of Earhart's plane.

ALI director Rick Pettigrew said the team was aware of the global interest in the expedition and would share its results "as soon as we are able". Purdue suggested before the poor weather hit that it could identify the Taraia Object in a matter of days.

blocks.caption: Map showing the relative locations of Papua New Guinea, Hawaii, Australia, Howland Island and Kikumaroro Island

blocks.text: While researchers have previously found evidence of a human presence on the island around the time of Earhart's disappearance, some skeptics believe the Taraia Object was just a tree that had fallen from the atoll into the lagoon.
Previous attempts to find her Electra have also come up short.

In 2024, a group of researchers said they may have found it lying around 4,877m (16,000ft) below the surface near Howland Island through sonar imaging - but this was later confirmed to be a rock formation.
Similarly, an expedition in 2019 to investigate a photograph of what might have been landing gear protruding from the water near Nikumaroro also failed to find anything.

blocks.caption: A satellite image of Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean showing the location of the Taraia Object

articles.title: France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
articles.summary: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left…

image.caption: Glucksmann has a difficult campaign ahead as the Socialist candidateImage: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: The historically working-class Parisian neighborhood of Belleville has gentrified in recent years. It was here that Raphael Glucksmann, a member of the European Parliament for France's center-left Socialists, celebrated his victory in the party's presidential primary on October 11.

Two rounds of voting had been anticipated, but the 46-year-old son of philosopher and essayist Andre Glucksmann triumphed in the first round with a convincing 66% of the vote and will be the Socialist candidate in France's 2027 presidential election.

As he left the Cantine de Belleville restaurant, Glucksmann was flour-bombed by an unidentified assailant. The following morning, he called on his rival, the left-wing French populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, to condemn attacks carried out by his supporters, though it is not clear that the attacker was indeed a supporter of Melenchon's La France Insoumise (LFI).
The incident has highlighted the issue set to dog Glucksmann's presidential candidacy over the coming weeks: How can he win over Melenchon's supporters if he refuses to work with their candidate?

blocks.caption: Glucksmann was flour-bombed while leaving his victory celebrationImage: Raphael Lafargue/abaca/picture alliance

blocks.text: Gluckmann's rapid rise

"Where do you stand on Melenchon?" That was the question that dominated much of the Socialists' primary campaign. Party leader Olivier Faure spoke in favor of leaving the door open for cooperation with the LFI, but Glucksmann called for a clear break with the far left. His decisive victory is therefore also seen as a vote in favor of a clear demarcation.

The other primary candidates questioned Glucksmann's political experience. Segolene Royal, a previous presidential candidate, compared his bid for the Elysee with that of an "intern" wanting to take charge of a company. She said Glucksmann had no experience in government or even running a local authority.

Despite Glucksmann's victory in the primary, his starting position is a difficult one. A poll by Toluna Harris Interactive, published the day after his win, projects that he would win 10–11% of the vote. The same poll put Melenchon on 18%, meaning the far-left man would be much more likely to reach the runoff. But the survey was conducted before Glucksmann won the primary, and so does not take into account any potential boost the nomination may give him. Still, 10% would be an improvement on the Socialists' performance in the last presidential election in 2022, when their candidate Anne Hidalgo won just 1.75% of the national vote.

There is also the complication that the Socialists are banking on a man who is not even a party member to lead them from irrelevance. Raphael Glucksmann actually belongs to a small center-left party called Place Publique.
France students demand better schools
Melenchon's youth appeal

Glucksmann has his work cut out for him — especially with young people. In an Ipsos survey in September, which posited Glucksmann as the social-democratic candidate and Edouard Philippe as the only candidate from the political center, Melenchon scored 41% among the under-25s. Meanwhile, 20% of this age group supported the far-right nationalist Marine Le Pen. France's young electorate is politically divided, but Melenchon still dominates on the left.

The 75-year-old is currently rallying alongside the students whose protests have drawn international attention. At a rally near Clermont-Ferrand in central France , he expressed solidarity with their movement and reiterated his calls for lowering the voting age to 16 and abolishing Parcoursup, France's national admissions procedure for higher education.

In an analysis for the Fondation Jean-Jaures, a Socialist-aligned think tank, the political scientist Antoine Bristielle distinguishes between a core group of committed LFI voters and the broader left. Melenchon's most loyal supporters, he says, are often young, educated city-dwellers, and many are under a lot of financial pressure. Four in ten households in this group live on a net monthly income of less than €2,000 ($2,200).

Bristielle estimates that just under a third of the left-wing electorate in his study care more about a left-wing victory than their allegiance to any particular party. Almost half of the people in this group are younger than 35, and would consider voting for the Socialists, the Greens, or LFI. Redistribution and an active government are important to them, but most would prefer politicians who are willing to compromise.

blocks.caption: Melenchon in Paris during a public sector strike on September 29Image: Tom Nicholson/REUTERS

blocks.text: Glucksmann's youth efforts

The pattern recently observed in Germany, where young women are more likely to vote for the left and young men for the right, does not apply in France. Political scientists Anja Durovic, Nonna Mayer and Noemie Piolat found that in the 2024 European and parliamentary elections, young French women were not significantly more likely to vote for the left, or less likely to vote for the far right, than men of the same age. It remains to be seen whether this pattern will be replicated in the 2027 presidential election.

Glucksmann says he would ease the burden on earned income by reducing France's CSG social security tax while increasing taxes on inheritances worth more than €2 million. He also presents himself as a committed supporter of European integration, while Melenchon has called the EU a neoliberal institution. Glucksmann's political profile combines social policy demands with foreign policy positions that could also appeal to voters from the camp of the current president, Emmanuel Macron.

France's Ukraine policy is one such issue. Glucksmann favors decisive support for Kyiv. Manon Aubry, a member of the European Parliament for Melenchon's LFI, says her party supports military assistance only under certain conditions, namely: The provision of aid to Ukraine must first be subject to democratic debate; it must not enable attacks deep inside Russian territory; and it must not weaken France's own defense capabilities. In 2024, LFI MPs voted against the French–Ukrainian security agreement.

The tension between the parties of the left was once again apparent in the aftermath of the flour attack in Belleville. The LFI MP Sebastien Delogu posted a declaration of support on X for the taxi driver who was going to have to clean his car.

Glucksmann must win over a lot of voters from Melenchon's camp if he is to have a chance of winning the presidency. This is likely to prove a much more difficult task than simply distancing himself from Melenchon.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: How AI is making it harder to book on Airbnb; Is junk food bad for your brain?: CBC's Marketplace Cheat Sheet
articles.summary: The CBC's Marketplace rounds up the consumer and health news you need from the week.

image.caption: Josh Wells noticed that text on an artwork in an Airbnb listing looked jumbled, which raised his suspicions that the image had been edited or generated using AI. (Josh Wells/Reddit)

blocks.text: Marketplace·New
The CBC's Marketplace rounds up the consumer and health news you need from the week.
The consumer news you may have missed this week
Miss something this week? Don't panic. The CBC's Marketplace rounds up the consumer and health news you need.
Want this in your inbox? Get the Marketplace newsletter every Friday.
Behind the lens: How Marketplace uses hidden cameras
(CBC)
This week's episode features an inside look at our hidden camera investigations, ranging from driving schools to real estate to social experiments.
Find out how we decide when to go undercover, why we do it and what it takes to uncover the truth — straight from some of the journalists who bring you the stories.
Watch the full episode anytime on YouTube or CBC Gem.
AI photos are making it harder to know what you're booking on Airbnb. Here's what to look out for

When booking his trip to Montreal, Wells found extremely polished-looking photos of hosts appeared in numerous Airbnb listings, leading him to suspect they had been generated using AI. Short-term rentals in that city are subject to strict rules aimed in part at protecting the city's housing supply. (Josh Wells/Reddit)

Josh Wells, a college student from Iowa, was excited to explore Montreal on his first trip outside the U.S. But as he scrolled through Airbnb listings in search of a place to stay, he began to notice something that didn't seem quite right.
Several of the hosts renting out their properties had profile pictures that Wells suspected were generated by artificial intelligence.
"Your average person taking an iPhone photo, there's obviously like a little bit of imperfections," Wells told the CBC's Cost of Living. "The AI photos, they just looked too perfect."
Still, Wells kept browsing. He was even close to booking one of the properties when a final look at the listing's photos raised another red flag.

He zoomed in on a piece of wall art depicting two halves of faces joined together. At the top, the artwork appeared to read "Picasso." But in another photo of the same room, taken from a different angle, the artwork looked different.
"The text was all warped and funky," he said. "I'm just like, 'Yeah, OK, this is AI."

That was enough to put Wells off the listing — and ultimately using Airbnb for this trip. Unable to tell whether the photos showed a real place or an AI-generated version, he opted for an apartment-style hotel instead.
"The fake profile picture is one thing, but listings of the actual place that you're staying at and spending thousands of dollars was an immediate no for me.”
Wells isn't the only traveller to question whether the photos found on Airbnb or similar short-term rental-style platforms accurately reflect reality.

As AI makes it easier to alter photos, experts say travellers may find it increasingly difficult to know whether Airbnb-style listings accurately reflect reality, raising questions about consumer trust and protections in Canada.

In a statement to CBC News, Airbnb said its rules require listings to be "accurately represented" and that the company may ask hosts to remove content that uses AI or other digital technology to "edit flaws, hide damage, add amenities or attributes that are not part of a listing, or otherwise materially misrepresent the listing."

The company further said it encourages guests to report misleading listings and that those who find a property that doesn't match its description can contact its 24/7 community support team. Under AirCover, Airbnb added, it may help guests find a similar place or provide a refund if the host can't resolve the issue.
We know junk food isn't healthy, but scientists are trying to determine if it's also bad for our brains
Ultra-processed foods could damage your brain: study
Most people have food in their fridges and cupboards that they know isn't the healthiest choice.

A box of chocolate chip cookies you grab for a bedtime snack. Instant noodles for when you can't be bothered to make dinner. Or that bag of ketchup chips you grabbed on a late night stroll home from the bar.

But it's not just guilty pleasures. Nearly half of the calories Canadians consume — 45.7 per cent on average, according to Statistics Canada — comes in the form of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) and includes everything from breakfast cereals to frozen meals.
Over the years, research has shown that UPFs can negatively impact everything from our weight to our cardiovascular health, and could even be linked to some types of cancer.

But a new study co-authored by two professors at Hamilton's McMaster University, published Thursday by JAMA Network Open, signals that our brains could also suffer as a result of consuming too many foods produced to be cheap and ready-to-eat.

The authors say that the people with the highest intake of UPFs in their diets may face an increased likelihood of experiencing changes to the brain that could serve as precursors for stroke, dementia and cognitive decline.
People wouldn't necessarily be aware of these potential harms, says study co-author Russell de Souza, an associate professor at McMaster's Mary Heersink School of Global Health and Social Medicine.
But he says the findings could encourage people to shift their eating habits now, before experiencing serious consequences later in life.

Bobby Hristova is an award-winning investigative reporter with CBC's Marketplace. He writes The Watchdog, Marketplace's weekly newsletter.
